newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan man hid father's body in pension fraud.
newsitem.headline: Japan man hid father's body in pension fraud.

text.p: A man who hid his dead father's body in their apartment for 2-1/2 years so he could collect his pension checks has been charged with fraud, a police spokesman said on Wednesday.

Masao Yanagisawa, 38, who police said admitted hiding the body of his father Masakatsu after he died from an illness at the age of 60 in July 1994, also hid the death from his sister and brother who had been supporting the two men.
Yanagisawa collected 3.5 million yen ($28,600) in pension checks, a police spokesman in western Tokyo told Reuters.
"We found out about it when Yanagisawa came to a local police station and confessed after his sister became suspicious about why their father was never home when she called," the spokesman said.
Yanagisawa, who is unemployed, said he wrapped his father's body in a plastic sheet when he died and hid it in a room of the apartment the two men shared.
"His sister, who lives close by, visited from time to time and became suspicious because the father was never at home, so she confronted Yanagisawa," the police spokesman said.
"It wasn't so much the pension fraud, it was deceiving his elder brother and sister. His older brother was giving him 80,000 yen ($655) a month, partly for their father's upkeep.
"Both the brother and sister are very angry with him about hiding their father's death," the added.
Yanagisawa faces a maximum sentence of 10 years in jail if found guilty of fraud. ($1=122 yen)
